column1: Updated assessment: The FOMC statement remains mildly positive—solid growth, easing inflation, and risks moving toward better balance, with policy on hold and QT continuing. But the July 2024 SLOOS indicates ongoing credit headwinds: banks continued to tighten standards for C&I and CRE loans and reported weaker demand across residential real estate (including government and GSE-eligible mortgages and HELOCs), credit cards, auto, and other consumer loans, alongside wider spreads and stricter terms (e.g., higher minimum scores/payments). Paired with FSR-flagged vulnerabilities (CRE stress, nonbank leverage, market liquidity strains, and fiscal concerns), these SLOOS findings temper the positive macro tone, even as bank funding and some securitization activity have stabilized. Net: cautiously positive, but more constrained by credit conditions than the initial read. sentiment score = 0.21
